title: workbench-text.v1
description: The third swappable pack, alongside presentation and layout: everything a person reads that is not domain data. Glyph tokens, format templates for derived readouts, and the message set. It exists because presentation text with no owner ends up hard-coded in the runtime and duplicated into authored surfaces, where it drifts from the data it claims to describe and cannot be verified, swapped or translated.

locale.description: BCP 47 tag. One pack, one locale.

glyphs.description: Every non-ASCII character the interface presents, named once. This is the only place such characters are authored, which is what makes a text-encoding check cheap and total instead of a hunt through string literals.

formats.description: Templates for values derived from the scene, the camera or a run. `{name}` placeholders are filled from supplied values and from glyphs. A readout is formatted here, never assembled by concatenation at the point of use, so the same fact cannot be phrased two ways in two places.

messages.description: Fixed text with no derived values. Includes the states a person must be able to tell apart: idle, unavailable, mismatched and unsupported are four different messages because they are four different facts.

playLabels.description: The playback affordance's label per lifecycle state. It cannot be a binding, because an action component declares no binding directions, so it is declared here rather than embedded in the runtime.

viewKindNames.description: Display name per source view kind. Previously a dictionary inside the build tool, which put presentation text in a place no profile could reach.

unresolvedTemplate.description: What to render when a template or placeholder is missing. It must be visibly wrong rather than silently empty: a blank readout looks like a legitimate absence of data.
